cases.question: Based on our pace and what's left, should we ask the client for more doors, or a second pass on the turf we have?

facts.name: doors we can knock in the days left

answer.question: Based on our pace and what's left, should we ask the client for more doors, or a second pass on the turf we have?
answer.answer:
Ask the client for more doors: at our current pace we will knock more doors than the untouched turf we have left, and new turf beats a second pass.
- Capacity for the rest of the program: 23826 doors (1489.1 a day times 16 days left) [table:v_office_pace]
- Untouched doors left in our turf: 10393 program-wide (Eastgate 1183, Harbor 8096, Northside 1114) [table:v_turf_summary]
- By office, capacity tops untouched turf in Eastgate (6091 vs 1183) and Northside (9936 vs 1114); Harbor still has more untouched doors than capacity (8096 vs 7798), so it keeps working its own turf [table:v_office_pace] [table:v_turf_summary]
- Even so the program projects 57329 doors, -3303 vs goal [table:v_office_pace]
- Rule: when capacity is larger than untouched doors, ask for more doors first; a second pass on the 18555 not-home doors is the fallback because second passes contact voters at roughly half the first-pass rate [doc:program-plan#more-doors-or-a-second-pass] [table:v_turf_summary]

answer.question: Why does the client's daily report show more doors than our dashboard for Oct 12?
answer.answer:
The client's sheet counts attempts before QC rollbacks, while our dashboard counts doors once per day with rollbacks removed; on Oct 12 most of the gap is Eastgate's 142 rolled-back flash-knocking attempts.

- All offices: 1484 attempts vs 1281 doors, 142 rolled back [table:v_daily_doors]
- The rollback is Jalen Ortiz's Eastgate shift flagged for flash knocking, 142 knocks, whole shift rolled back [table:v_qc_flags_detail]
- The gap = repeat attempts at the same door plus rolled-back attempts; rollbacks happen after the day's report is pulled [doc:counting-doors#why-the-client-s-numbers-differ-from-ours] [doc:client-reporting#daily-report]

cases.question: What counts as flash knocking under our QC rules?

answer.question: What counts as flash knocking under our QC rules?
answer.answer:
Flash knocking is recording doors faster than a person can walk to them and knock; a shift is flagged when 10 or more consecutive knocks are recorded less than 30 seconds apart.
- Threshold: 10 or more consecutive knocks under 30 seconds apart [doc:qc-rules#flash-knocking]
- Confirmed flash knocking is rolled back, so those knocks no longer count as doors or contacts; a whole shift recorded this way is rolled back in full [doc:qc-rules#flash-knocking]
- Rolled-back knocks stay in the data marked rolled back, and rollbacks never change a client report already sent [doc:counting-doors#rollbacks]
- An open flag needs a conversation with the field lead before the canvasser's next shift; two or more in one week go to the field director [doc:qc-rules#what-happens-after-a-flag]

sources.text: Flash knocking is recording doors faster than a person can walk to them and knock. A shift is flagged when 10 or more consecutive knocks are recorded less than 30 seconds apart. Confirmed flash knocking is rolled back: the knocks in the window no longer count as doors or contacts. A whole shift recorded this way is rolled back in full.

When QC confirms flash knocking, the knocks in the flagged window are rolled back: they stay in the data with rolled_back = true but are removed from doors and contacts. Rollbacks happen after the day's client report has been pulled, so they never change a report that was already sent.

Every open flag needs a conversation between the field lead and the canvasser before the canvasser's next shift, using the timestamped evidence on the flag. After the conversation the flag is marked reviewed. Two or more householding or flash knocking flags in one week for the same canvasser go to the field director.

sources.text: When projected capacity for the rest of the program (average daily doors of the last 7 days times days left) is larger than the untouched doors left in our turf, we will run out of first-pass turf. In that case ask the client for more doors first; new turf contacts voters at the normal first-pass rate. A second pass on not-home doors is the fallback, because second passes contact voters at roughly half the first-pass rate. If untouched doors exceed capacity, keep working the turf we have.
